So, about my team, let me explain the whole situation, because I think the context matters. In March we took on the Chile portfolio. Nobody left the team, so on paper nothing changed, but the volume of files grew by about a third. In April and May we managed with overtime. In June one analyst went on holiday and we stopped answering inside the agreed time. I spoke to my director, and at first we discussed two new positions. Then we looked at the numbers again and, honestly, two is not realistic this year. So today the team asked for one replacement, not two new positions. One more thing, and this is why I keep calling you. I have two good candidates in the process right now, and if the decision waits until January, I lose both of them.

Claire, ninety seconds on the credit team, if you have them. Some background first: in March the team took on the Chile portfolio and the volume grew by about a third, with the same number of people. Now the key point. Today they asked for one replacement, not the two new positions we discussed in June. My recommendation is to approve the replacement now and to review the second position in January, because the role is inside the approved budget and the workload is documented. It depends on one thing: finance confirms the budget on Friday. Next steps, then. Finance confirms on Friday, I speak to the manager the same day, and the candidate process continues in parallel. That is everything.
